pathways.climate_pressure: Historical severe drought affecting staple production in Dry Corridor communities.
pathways.documented_impact: Smallholder harvest and livelihood losses in the programme context examined in 2019.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Low cohesion, gang-related social control and negotiated programme access can narrow collective coping and participation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Combined livelihood stress and access restrictions may undermine resilience; no causal claim that drought created gangs or a quantified increase in violence.
alternative_explanations: Civil-war legacies, land inequality, economic exclusion, gang governance and wider political dynamics independently affect insecurity.
pathways.uncertainty: Qualitative programme research from March 2019, not current territorial-control evidence or an estimated climate effect. Fieldwork sites are not a uniform risk ranking.
resilience_factors: The study observed communication between workers, smallholders, landowners and authorities; these reported contributions to cohesion are not an independently identified peace impact.
pathways.compact_statement: In historical Dry Corridor programme settings, drought-related harvest loss overlapped with low cohesion and gang restrictions that constrained coping and programme access; climate causation of gang violence is not established.

gaps: March 2019 gang and programme-access findings are historical; they do not describe the materially different 2026 security context.
Field-visit municipalities are not assigned identical gang restrictions. No source establishes that drought caused gang formation or measures a climate-attributable violence rate.

executive_assessment.text: Historical assessments identify Dry Corridor agricultural dependence and named high-vulnerability departments, alongside metropolitan flood and landslide exposure.
The 2019 SIPRI/WFP research describes drought, weak cohesion and gang restrictions on programme participation; these are local historical mechanisms, not a current national climate–violence estimate.
